refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: This server is intended to be started at system start up time. It attaches a consumer to every ringbuffer that has been and will be created and monitors the throughput in total bytes, total physics items (events) as well as bytes/events since the last begin run item. It also computes rates of bytes and events per second.

The server advertises with the NSCLDAQ port manager as the service: RING_MONITOR. Connecting to that service results in the monitor spitting out the statistics in JSON format (see STATISTICS FORMAT below). After providing the statistics, the ring monitor willl shutdown the connection to the client.

If the optional stats-log-file command parameter is supplied, it must be a file path that either points into a writable directory or points to a writable sqlite3 database file. Periodically, statistics will be written to that file. If omitted, statistics will not be written. See STATISTICS DATABASE SCHEMA below for the database schema.

A word about the ring monitor structure that is important. The NSCLDAQ ringmaster reacts to the destruction of a ringbuffer by attempting to kill processes that are attached to the ringbuffer either as the producer or a consumer. THerefore, the ringmonitor is actually a pair of processes. The parent process starts the actual monitor program and, when it exits, restarts it. This implies that deleting a ringbuffer resets the statistics on all rings. This also implies that while the monitor program needs, and does react to the creation of new ringbuffers, it does not need to react to the destruction of ringbuffers as the ringmaster will force a restart, which will re-inventory the rings.
The rng monitor program does not restrict the set of hosts that can connect to it. This implies that ring statistics can be moniotored from non DAQ nodes.

refsect1.title: STATISTICS FORMAT
refsect1.para: The ring monitor returns statistics to clients in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON). See for a description of JSON. Fortunately, JSON decoding libraries exist for many programming languages. FRIB containers provide JSON decoding libraries for several languages. This section describes the JSON that the ring monitor returns. The server returns an array of JSON objects. each object provides statistics for a single ringbuffer. The proxy rings that represent remote ringbuffer are included in the array.
Below is an example of an idle system with a single ring named ring2 that has never had data produced into it. I have prettified the JSON to make it more readable.

If there were additional ring buffers, they would be separated from the structure shown additional each other by commas, per JSON array notation. The object that describes ring buffer statistics has the following attributes:

listitem.para: The name of the ringbuffer. Note this is a local ringbuffer name, not a URI.
An object that describes the cumulative statistics fromt he ring. These are the statistics since the last restart of the ring monitor. The attributes of this object will be described below.
Instantaneous bytes per second through the ring.
Instantaneous rate of PHYSICS_EVENT items through the ringbuffers.
Same as byte_rate once a run is stable. At the start of the run there may be a perturbation.
Same as event_rate though there can be a downward perturbation at the start of the run.

refsect1.para: The cum_statistics is itelf an object which has the following attributes:

listitem.para: The name of the ring buffer again.
Number of bytes that have gone through the ringbuffer since the server started.
Number of PHYSICS_EVENT ring items that have gone through the ring sinc the server was started.
Number of bytes that have gone through the ring buffers since the most recent BEGIN_RUN item was observed.
Number of PHYSICS_EVENT ring items that were observed since the most recent BEGIN_RUN was observed.

refsect1.para: Note: The countes for the run begin counting when the server starts and don't wait for a begin run item. Thus if the server is started in the middle of the run, the counters and rates will be from the start of the server until a BEGIN_RUN is observed at which time the totals for a run will be reset.

refsect1.title: STATISTICS DATABASE SCHEMA
refsect1.para: Statistics are logged, if requested, into two tables, which are created as follows:

informalexample.programlisting: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ring_names ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name STRING ) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statistics ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, ring_id INTEGER, -- FK to ring_names timestamp STRING, volume INTEGER, -- Total bytes run_vol INTEGER, -- bytes this run events INTEGER, -- total events. run_events INTEGER, -- events this run. rate REAL, -- bytes/per second. event_rate REAL -- Events/second. )

refsect1.para: The ring_names table contains one entry for each ringbuffer file that has been seen by the server. The name (not path or URI) is stored in the name field and the id primary key is used as a foreign key in the statistics table.
The statistics table is where the statistics are stored. Each update provides a timstamped entry:

listitem.para: Is a unique primary key for each record.
Is a foreign key into the ring_names table indicating to which ring buffer, this statistic entry belongs.

Is a timestamp field in RFC 3339 ISO 8601 date/time format. In this format, 2025-11-04T08:57:44.270119696-05:00 represents November 4, 2025 8:57:44AM (and change) in a timezome 5 hours behind GMT (EST).
The total data volume in bytes observed to pass through the ringbuffer since the server started.
The data volume in bytes observed to pass through the ring buffer since the most recent BEGIN_RUN ring item (or server start if data was flowing at the time the server started).
Total number of PHYSICS_EVENT ring items observed in the ringbuffer since the server started.
Number of PHYSICS_EVENT ring items observed in the ring buffer since the most rcent BEGIN_RUN item.
The instantaneous of data through the ring buffer in bytes/sec.
The instantaneous rate of PHYSICS_EVENT items through the ring buffer as items/sec.

refsect1.title: BUGS
refsect1.para: WHen a ringbuffer is deleted, the ring master, in the system the ringbuffer lived in will kill all clients (producer and consumers) that are attached to that ring. This means that the ring_monitor will be killed as well. The ring_monitor, however consists of a parent process that spawns off the actual monitor and, when the actual monitor exits restarts it. Unfortunately that means that all counters maintained by the ring_monitor are reset when a ringbuffer is deleted. This is not expected to be fixed.
